snapshot.title: Contact data enrichment: external data into fields, AI context, and signals
snapshot.author: KhaiStimpson
snapshot.body:
Implements the contact data enrichment feature end to end, per the design brief in `docs/specs/contact-data-enrichment.md`. External data (company website, news, AU/NZ registries, optional paid person data) enriches contacts through **one ingestion pipeline with three sinks** — all gated by a per-tenant admin opt-in, all sourced, and nothing touches a contact field without human confirmation.

> Consolidates the earlier design-brief PR (#57, now closed) — the brief and its housekeeping are included here, so this is the single PR for the feature.

## What it does

- **Free-first providers** behind a common `IEnrichmentProvider` seam:
  - `CompanyWebsiteEnrichmentProvider` — OG/meta from the email domain → company, logo, description.
  - `NewsSignalProvider` — Google News RSS by company, with a headline-match relevance gate.
  - `AbrAbnProvider` (AU) / `NzbnProvider` (NZ) — official business registries, matched by company name with a conservative confidence gate. **Config-gated** (`Enrichment:Abr:Guid` / `Enrichment:Nzbn:ApiKey`): inert until their credential is set.
  - `PeopleDataLabsProvider` — optional paid person-level enrichment via a per-tenant **BYO key** (stored DataProtection-encrypted).
- **Three sinks:** field findings → `EnrichmentSuggestion` (suggest-then-confirm, mirroring `Commitment`); knowledge → `ExternalKnowledge`, a citable AI retrieval source (`AiSourceKind.ExternalKnowledge`); signals → a timeline `Activity` **and** knowledge, with notable ones also becoming a Today-digest `RecommendationKind.EnrichmentSignal`.
- **Surfaces:** an "Enrich" button + review panel on the contact page; signals in the relationship timeline; notable signals in the Today digest; an admin opt-in toggle on both the General and AI-governance settings tabs, plus the BYO-key field.
- **Automation:** auto-enrich on contact create and CSV/vCard import (Hangfire, gated + bounded); a daily scheduled refresh that re-enriches a bounded, stalest-first slice per tenant.
- **AI integration:** enriched knowledge flows into the Relationship Brief through the existing PII gateway and is authorized by `AiSourceAuthorizationService`. Selection is factored behind `IExternalKnowledgeSelector` (the RAG seam) so a future vector top-k selector can replace today's bounded recency inclusion without touching treatments.

## Privacy & governance

Off by default; explicit tenant-admin opt-in, re-checked before every fetch; every run audited (`EnrichmentAuditEvent`). Field changes only apply on human accept. External knowledge is tokenised by the PII gateway like any other source. BYO keys are encrypted at rest.

## Testing

~150 enrichment unit tests (parsers, provider mapping, relevance/confidence gates, fail-soft, routing/dedupe, opt-in gating, scheduler selection, RAG seam). Full suite: **307 passing**. The only failures are 4 pre-existing Playwright browser-binary tests, unchanged by this branch. Key flows were also driven end-to-end in the running app (Enrich → accept, timeline signal, Today digest, BYO-key encryption).

## Notes for reviewers

- Dual Sqlite + SqlServer EF migrations included for each schema change.
- New config keys documented in the README.
- **NZBN** parser is verified field-by-field against the official OpenAPI spec (`/entities` search: `nzbn`, `entityName`, `entityTypeDescription`, `entityStatusDescription`; `Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key` header) — ready to go live once the key is set.
- **ABR** is built to the documented JSONP `*.aspx` endpoints (callback param sent, envelope unwrapped); a live smoke is pending the GUID being provisioned, and a small field-name tweak may be needed at first real call.
- Deferred by design: a per-tenant enrichment spend governor (v1 uses a slow rolling cadence + per-run cap instead) and the vector RAG selector (seam is in place).

reviewPointAdded.title: Doesn't surface failures as ProviderOperationException
reviewPointAdded.summary: 5 new or changed classes (AbrAbnProvider, CompanyWebsiteEnrichmentProvider, NewsSignalProvider and 2 more) don't report failures by throwing ProviderOperationException, unlike 5 of 7 classes that take HttpClient in this repository.
reviewPointAdded.whyItMatters: Most classes that take HttpClient here report failures by throwing ProviderOperationException — for example ClickSendClient, GraphMailService, MailgunClient and 2 more. AbrAbnProvider catches exceptions broadly without rethrowing instead. Following the established approach keeps behaviour predictable for callers and makes the code easier to reason about alongside its peers. There are exceptions (AzureAiProvider and AzureOpenAiTranscriptionService), so this may be deliberate — worth confirming.
reviewPointAdded.suggestedComment: Other classes that take HttpClient in this repo (ClickSendClient, GraphMailService, MailgunClient and 2 more) report failures by throwing ProviderOperationException. Should these follow the same approach rather than catching and handling failures locally, or is the difference intentional here?

reviewPointAdded.title: Doesn't call AppDbContext.SaveChangesAsync
reviewPointAdded.summary: EnrichmentScheduler doesn't call AppDbContext.SaveChangesAsync, unlike 13 of 16 classes that take IBackgroundJobClient in this repository.
reviewPointAdded.whyItMatters: Most classes that take IBackgroundJobClient here call AppDbContext.SaveChangesAsync — for example VoiceNotesController, NewModel, DetailModel and 10 more. Following the established approach keeps behaviour predictable for callers and makes the code easier to reason about alongside its peers. There are exceptions (GraphConnectController, WebhooksController and WebhookInboxProcessor), so this may be deliberate — worth confirming.
